turns.patient_opening: Hi. I’m a 6-year-old boy. I’ve had intense coughing fits and when I cough or strain (like trying to lift something heavy or force a bowel movement), my stomach area hurts a lot—mostly on the right side near the groin/right lower belly. My tummy feels bloated too, and I also have a pale red skin spot there that looks swollen, bigger than 1 cm.

turns.doctor_question: Is the affected area located on the **right labia majora** (the outer fold of skin on the right side of the vulva)?
turns.patient_answer: I think it’s on the right side, but I’m not sure it’s on the labia majora exactly. It feels more like the right lower belly/groin area near the right iliac fossa.

turns.doctor_question: Is the affected area located in your **upper gum**? (yes/no)
Do you currently have a fever—either that you feel (hot/flushed) or that you’ve measured with a thermometer?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t have a fever that I feel or that we measured.

turns.doctor_question: Do your skin lesions peel off or flake away (for example, like dry skin coming off)?
turns.patient_answer: No, they don’t peel or flake away.

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have painful mouth ulcers or sores (like canker sores)?
Do you feel so tired that you’re unable to do your usual activities, or are you stuck in bed all day long?
turns.patient_answer: No, I’m not stuck in bed all day. I’m mostly uncomfortable because of the coughing and the pain, but I can still do some things.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been diagnosed with pericarditis (inflammation around the heart)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I’ve never been diagnosed with pericarditis.

turns.doctor_question: Are you consulting today because you’ve been told you have high blood pressure?
turns.patient_answer: No. I haven’t been told I have high blood pressure.
